newsitem.title: USA: Georgia Power to call Class A preferreds.
newsitem.headline: Georgia Power to call Class A preferreds.

text.p: Southern Co said on Tuesday its Georgia Power unit would call in its 1.90 Class A preferred shares.

In a separate statement, Southern Co also said that through its Southern Energy Inc subsidiary, it reached a long-term agreement with Dominion Companies to act as the luxury apartment developer's energy provider and consultant.

Georgia Power said it planned to redeem, on January 2, 1997, all oustanding shares of its $1.90 class A preferreds with a $25 stated value at the redemption price of $25 per share plus accrued dividends to the date of redemption.
The books would be closed on the redemption date, the company said.

Georgia Power said it also authorized redemption on January 2, 1997 of all its $60.26 million outstanding 8-5/8 percent First Mortgage Bonds due June 1, 2022 at the special redemption price equal to the principal amount plus accrued interest to the date of redemption, without premium.
Georgia Power would use a combination of cash proceeds of released property and cash deposited in satisfaction of the Improvement Fund to redeem these bonds, it said.
Under provisions of the company's bond indenture, proceeds from the sale of the property and funds deposited by operation of the Improvement Fund may be used to redeem bonds at par, the company said.
Regarding its agreement with Dominion, Southern Co said it had exclusive right to provide energy to all of Dominion's properties, where it could legally provide such a service.

Southern and Dominion already worked as partners at the Chatelaine Park apartment community in Duluth, Georgia. This new agreement also allowed Southern to coordinate services similar to Chatelaine's at communities of Dominion's choosing, the company said.
The companies worked together at Chatelaine with other partners on a pilot program to bring services to residents under a unified bill.
